Definition: a bunch of grapes or other fruit
BiblicalUsage: ʼEshkôwl is a cluster — a bunch of grapes, the fruit hanging together. The spies carry a cluster from Eshcol so large that two men bear it on a staff; the cupbearer's dream shows clusters ripening on the vine; and the grapes of the wicked are bitter. It is the word for fruit in abundance.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ʼeshkôwl is the picture of the promised land's fruitfulness: one cluster, and it takes two men to carry it. I hold that the fruit God promises is always more than I can carry alone.
